en: Petavatthu,
Cūḷavagga 7.
The Story of the Deer-Hunter Ghost (Migaluddakapetavatthu)
“Surrounded by men and women, a youth,
you shine with delightful strands of sensual pleasure;
you enjoy the cause for a day.”
“What did you do in a previous birth?
[He replied: “In delightful Rājagaha, in the charming Giribbaja;”
In the past, I was a deer-hunter,
cruel and with blood-stained hands,
toward living beings who offered no resistance.
With a mind corrupted toward many beings,
I wandered always most cruelly,
delighting in harming others and unrestrained.
I had a companion, a kind-hearted,
faithful lay follower;
out of compassion for me, he too—
He restrained him again and again:
“Do not commit evil deeds;
do not, my dear, go to a state of misery.”
“If you desire happiness after passing away,
refrain from killing living beings and from lack of self-restraint.
Having heard his words, I—
Though he desired my happiness and was compassionate for my welfare,
I, lacking wisdom and delighting in long-standing evil,
did not follow his complete instruction.
Then, out of compassion, that one of vast wisdom established me again in self-restraint, saying:
"If you kill living beings by day,..."
"Then may you have self-restraint during the night.
"By day I have killed living beings,
but at night I am abstinent and self-controlled."
At night I enjoy my pleasures,
but by day I am devoured, fallen into misery.
Of that wholesome karma...
I experience a non-human state at night;
by day, dogs, being driven off,
run at me from all sides to devour me.
And those who are constantly devoted, firmly applied to the teaching of the Sugata—
I consider them to have attained the Deathless alone.
They attain the unconditioned state.
The Story of the Deer-Hunter Petas, the Seventh.
